title: Maybe
description:
Write `Maybe<T>`: a value that might not be there. (The standard library's version is `std::optional`; building a simple one shows there is no magic in it.)

| Member | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `Maybe()` | empty |
| `Maybe(T value)` | holds the value (not `explicit`, so a function returning `Maybe<int>` can `return 5;`) |
| `bool hasValue() const` | |
| `const T& value() const` | the value; throws `std::logic_error` if empty |
| `T valueOr(T fallback) const` | the value, or the fallback if empty |
| `void reset()` | becomes empty |
| `template <typename F> auto map(F function) const` | if there is a value, returns a `Maybe` holding `function(value)`; if empty, an empty `Maybe` of that result type |

Storing a `T` plus a `bool` flag is fine (so `T` must be default-constructible).
hints: Store a `bool m_has{ false };` and a `T m_value{};`. `value()` checks `m_has` and throws `std::logic_error` when it is false.

For `map`, call the function on the value when there is one and wrap the result in a `Maybe` of its type: `using R = decltype(function(m_value)); return m_has ? Maybe<R>{ function(m_value) } : Maybe<R>{};`.
